flawed_step: Lines 0006–0007 claim uniqueness of the transitive reduction implies acyclicity.
counterexample: Let G have one vertex v and the single edge (v,v). Then G is cyclic. Its transitive closure is {(v,v)}. Any graph on {v} with this transitive closure must contain (v,v), since paths must have positive length; the empty graph has no such path. Hence G's unique transitive reduction is itself.
assessment_summary: The claimed equivalence fails because self-loops are not excluded by the stated graph assumptions.
